chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Salt, Abu al-'Udayis, from Salih, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Salih, follow the one who makes you weep while he is sincere to you, and do not follow the one who makes you laugh while he is deceptive to you. You will all return to Allah, and then you will know.'
ai.seo_question: How can one distinguish between a sincere friend and a deceptive one according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a profound criterion for evaluating companionship by linking emotional response to spiritual truth: the sincere friend (*nasih*) induces weeping through humility and remembrance of God, while the deceptive friend (*ghashsh*) induces laughter through worldly distraction. This distinction is grounded in the eschatological reality of the 'Return' (*al-Rudd*), where all individuals will be held accountable for their true nature, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (awareness of God) in social interactions.
